text:
marie: Quick ask — we need a compact QA protocol + reproducible bench artifacts from runtime for the keynote demo (onstage live) next Tue. Can runtime produce a minimal bench sweep and a 10-sample 'smoke pack' (raw traces + CSV latencies) by EOD tomorrow? We'll use them in slides and the live fallback flow.

sam-runtime: Yep. To scope this down: which exact model, sequence lengths, and do you want quantized variants included? Also confirm whether to include KV/prefix caching or coldstart-only numbers.

marie: Target model family: redwood/opt-6.7b (baseline). Two seq lengths: short=128, long=2048. Prefer coldstart-focused (no prefix caching). For samples: ideal 100 warmup + 300 main per seq len; fallback to 50/150 if capacity/time. Include non-quant and 4-bit quant runs (if quant adds < 3h). We need p50/p90/p99, a coldstart heatmap, and a per-token cost estimate.

anya: I can own the acceptance criteria from the marketing side. Please make sure the artifacts include: CSV of per-request latencies, a percentile summary, and a short reproducible notebook. We need p99 for short < 600ms and p99 for long < 3s on the keynote backend; if we can't hit that, we'll show relative deltas rather than absolute claims.

sam-runtime: Understood. EOD tomorrow is tight but doable if we limit to one GPU flavor and no long retries. Quantized 4-bit runs may add time; if they push past the window we'll surface the results as a follow-up. We'll push artifacts to S3 and drop links here. Preliminary run command I'm going to use: 

```bash
rwd bench run --model redwood/opt-6.7b --seqs 128,2048 --warmup 100 --samples 300 --no-cache --gpu A100 --output s3://redwood-internal/keynote/1758001234/
```

sam-runtime: We'll also add a minimal repro payload and a tiny Jupyter snippet to reproduce the plots locally. Example snippet (placeholder): 

```python
# load latency CSV and compute percentiles
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('latency.csv')
percentiles = df['latency_ms'].quantile([0.5,0.9,0.99])
print(percentiles)
```

ellen: Also need per-route token cost breakdown (tokens in/out) and the anonymized request/response export so we can validate messaging examples. Can you tag the S3 runs with 'keynote-2026' and 'no-cache'?

runtime-bot: New bench task created: rtask-674321 — logs streaming: https://internal.logs/rtask-674321

sam-runtime: Confirming tagging and anonymization. Deliverables we'll produce: 1) raw per-request latency CSV, 2) percentile summary JSON, 3) coldstart heatmap PNG, 4) S3 folder with traces + run metadata + exact run command, 5) small repro notebook and a brief README describing methodology and any deviations. If quant runs fail or time out we'll include the status in the metadata and a note about expected delta.

marie: Perfect — one more request: add a single-line field in the run metadata that states whether requests used batching and the batch sizes (we want to be explicit in the slide callouts).

sam-runtime: Will do. I'll post the S3 link here when uploads complete.

runtime-bot: Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-internal/keynote/1758001234/ (latency.csv, percentiles.json, heatmap.png, traces.tar.gz, repro-notebook.ipynb) — https://s3.internal/keynote/1758001234/

marie: Amazing, thank you! :tada:

sam-runtime: Happy to help. If you need an abbreviated slide-ready CSV (p50/p90/p99 per slice) say the word and we'll attach it.

ellen: Please do — a small single-sheet CSV with the percentiles + per-token cost will be perfect for the keynote deck.

sam-runtime: Adding that now, will update the same S3 folder.

marie: Closing the loop — this is exactly what we needed. We'll QA the artifacts and circle back with any follow-ups.
